name: Rebound and Outlet
idea: Box out and grab the rebound, then throw a quick pass to a guard on the side to start a fast break.
why: Right after a rebound, the other team is still near your basket. A fast pass to a teammate waiting on the side, called an outlet pass, gets the ball up the court before they can get back, and that's how fast breaks start.
tryit: Rebounder: grab it with two hands, chin it, and turn to the sideline. Guard: as soon as you see the rebound, run to the side of the court near the free-throw line and call for the ball.

frames.say: You’re on defense. {1} is about to shoot. When a shot goes up, every red player's job is the rebound.
{1} shoots and misses! {X5} *boxes out*: back to {5}, so {5} can't get to the ball.
{X5} grabs the rebound with two hands. Now red has the ball!
{X5} turns toward the sideline, and {X1} runs to the side of the court and calls for the ball.
*Outlet pass:* {X5} throws it out to {X1}, right away.
{X1} dribbles up the court fast, and {X2} and {X5} race up too. Rebound, outlet, go: that's how a fast break starts!
